title: Gem
description: A gemstone used for ENGRAVING items — distinct from enchanting. Engraving adds NO effects of its own. Instead the dominant gem (by quality, or by quantity) OVERWRITES the engraved item's element (phase): e.g. a ruby makes a wooden sword Fire, which then interacts through the five-phase cycles in data/wuxing. An engraved item also gains a bonus to the magnitude of effects later enchanted onto it — that bonus comes from the gem's `tier` (see data/tiers). A gem TYPE is defined by its `phase` (element) and `tier` (Common→Legendary rarity, the source of truth for numbers). Quality (the qualityGrade ladder petty→grand) is NOT part of the definition: it varies between individual stones and is assigned per instance. NOT defined here: socket count (an item-side concern), and exactly how the tier bonus and per-instance quality are consumed by recipes (specified by the crafting / magic-crafting modules).

phase.description: The element this gem imparts. Required — engraving overwrites the item's element with the dominant gem's phase, which then resolves through the cycles in data/wuxing.

tier.description: Rarity tier — references an id in data/tiers (the source of truth). The tier supplies the gem's engraving bonus (effectMagnitude) and relative value; do not restate those numbers here.
